title: Chapter 22 — The Luxury Brand Landscape
intro: The luxury tier mapped — brand stories, design philosophies, and honest comparisons.

sections.title: The Luxury Tier Map
sections.content:
Luxury appliances occupy a different market than everything below them. The customer is not comparing a Sub-Zero to a Samsung — they are comparing Sub-Zero to Miele to Thermador. Your job is to navigate within the tier, not defend the tier's existence.

Sub-Zero Group (Sub-Zero, Wolf, Cove): American-made, Wisconsin heritage, strongest brand recognition among designers and architects. Known for food preservation technology (dual compressors, air purification) and the Wolf infrared broiler. Cove dishwashers complete the ecosystem.

Miele: German engineering, 20-year tested lifespan, and a reputation for reliability that borders on legendary. Their laundry, dishwashing, and coffee systems are world-class. Less designer-specified in North America than Sub-Zero/Wolf but growing.

Thermador (BSH): The One-Two-Free rebate program is a powerful selling tool. Star Burner design is distinctive. Freedom refrigeration columns are panel-ready. Strong integration with the Bosch ecosystem.

Gaggenau (BSH): Ultra-luxury, European aesthetic, commercial-grade performance. The 400 series is for the customer who wants a restaurant kitchen at home. Very limited distribution — exclusivity is the brand positioning.

sections.title: Honest Comparisons
sections.content:
At the luxury tier, every brand has legitimate strengths. Do not position one as universally 'best.' Position each as best for a specific customer profile.

The serious home cook who prioritizes cooking performance: Wolf or Gaggenau. The design-forward customer who wants everything to disappear behind panels: Sub-Zero columns with Miele integration. The customer who values the rebate program and ecosystem simplicity: Thermador. The customer who wants proven longevity and European build quality: Miele.

Be honest about weaknesses too. Every brand has them. The rep who volunteers an honest trade-off earns more trust than the one who claims perfection.

sections.title: The Designer Factor
sections.content:
At the luxury tier, designers heavily influence brand selection. Know which brands your local design community prefers and why. In some markets, Sub-Zero/Wolf dominates designer specs. In others, Thermador or Miele has stronger designer relationships.

Your relationship with designers determines which luxury brands move off your floor. Invest in the designer relationship and the luxury sales follow.
